counterexample: Take m = 5, n = 4, so S = {5, 6, 7, 8} and m^(4 rising) = 5*6*7*8 = 1680. Line 0025 asserts the product of the n elements of S can be written as k_1 * (2 k_2) * (3 k_3) * (4 k_4) with the n listed factors being the n elements of S, one designated multiple per j. That is impossible here: the only multiple of 4 in S is 8, the only multiple of 3 is 6, and the only remaining multiples of 2 are 6 and 8, both already used, so no system of distinct representatives exists. The claimed factorization of the product therefore does not exist for these values, even though 4! = 24 does divide 1680 (1680 = 24 * 70). The step is thus a non sequitur: the guarantee from lines 0011-0019 is only that S contains SOME multiple of each j, not that these multiples are distinct elements whose product exhausts S.
reasoning_summary: Lines 0001-0007 (definition of S, |S| = n) are fine. Lines 0009-0017 correctly invoke the lemma that any j successive integers contain a multiple of j, applied to the initial segments {m, ..., m+j-1} for j = 1..n (the ProofWiki wording 'contains a factor of j' means 'contains a multiple of j'; harmless terminology slip). Line 0019, read as 'for each j in 1..n, S contains a multiple of j', is a valid consequence. The failure is at lines 0021-0025: multiplying all elements of S and equating the product to k_1 * 2 k_2 * 3 k_3 * ... * n k_n silently assumes the n designated multiples are n DISTINCT elements of S, i.e. that a system of distinct representatives exists pairing each j in 1..n with its own element of S divisible by j. Nothing proved so far gives distinctness — one element can be the only available multiple for several different j (e.g. j = 2 and j = 4), and no element is available for the remaining j. Concretely for m = 5, n = 4 no such assignment exists, so the asserted equation is false as written. Consequently the extraction of the common factor n! in lines 0028-0032 is unjustified, and the conclusion at 0035-0038, though true (the standard proof goes via the integrality of binomial coefficients), is not established. Stopped at line 0025.
